title: Choose the eyes
question: Four directions for the animated eyes on the keyboard's home screen, each shown as the real 96x64 animation at 6x. Keep the lead, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Ping-Pong
options.lineage: puppet workshop: ping-pong ball eyes on felt
options.thesis: Two glossy balls on red felt with pupils that have weight: they overshoot, go cross-eyed, roll, and get a deadpan half-lid.
options.viewport: A solid red strip with a face that fills it; the only direction with a coloured ground and a sense of humour.
options.risk: The red ground is loud next to the home page's own readouts, and a comic character may wear thin on a work desk.

raised.raise: Pupils now move on a damped spring, so every glance settles physically instead of snapping.

options.label: Happy Mac
options.lineage: 1984 Macintosh startup icon, one-bit pixel drawing
options.thesis: A strict black-and-white face on a coarse pixel grid that blinks, glances, winks and dissolves in a dither.
options.viewport: White blocks on black: a face with a nose and a smile, readable from across the desk.
options.risk: The most familiar idea on the table for a Mac keyboard, and it uses none of the screen's colour.

options.label: Tide Glow
options.lineage: bioluminescent plankton on a night sea
options.thesis: Eyes made of hundreds of drifting motes of blue light; a blink spills them downward as a wake before they gather again.
options.viewport: Two soft clouds of twinkling light on near-black, always slightly in motion.
options.case: The most alive and the least like a cartoon; loses some clarity because the eye shapes are soft.
options.risk: At arm's length the motes can read as blue smudges rather than eyes.

options.label: Six-Pack
options.thesis: Two instrument dials whose radium-green needles do the looking; when the eyes disagree an amber caution lamp lights, and a blink is the instrument flag dropping.
options.viewport: Two gauges side by side on a black panel, needles sweeping with damped motion.
options.case: Fits a command screen best and stays calm beside the readouts; less of a character than the others.
options.risk: Reads as two clocks before it reads as eyes.

canonCard.label: Companion
canonCard.thesis: The rounded robot eyes this kind of screen usually ships with, in cyan, done cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Two glowing rounded rectangles that blink and glance.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the stock look by design.
